text: SitRep62 Tableau 6: 725 in isolation at end of day (281 confirmed / 444 suspected) at 85.6% global bed occupancy; Nord-Kivu 118.8% saturation, Ituri 79.0%, Tshopo 41.7%. Exits over 24h (117 total): 14 deaths, 75 non-cases, 13 recoveries, 13 escapes, 2 HGR transfers; 124 admissions. J-1 bed count 718. The bed identity closes exactly: 718 + 124 - 117 = 725. Saturation persists at CT Bambu (316%) and CTE CME Rwampara (157%). Sud-Kivu and Haut-Uele report no isolation structures this cycle.

Mahagi sits on the Goli-Mahagi cross-border axis toward Arua (Uganda); INSP explicitly ties the confirmation to elevated cross-border propagation risk and calls for reinforced PoE screening and contact tracing in the border zones.

text: Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) reached 50 consecutive days with no new confirmed case and leaves the active-transmission set: 46 zones touched, 45 active. Ituri holds 89.6% of cumulative confirmed cases and 80.4% of the last 24h of confirmations. Ituri's alert-investigation rate fell to 28.1% (133/474), the weakest of the outbreak, while three Ituri health zones (Bunia, Kambala, Mahagi) filed no contact-follow-up report.

text: reticence_post_mortem - Community reluctance toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs) and community resistance delay confirmation, underestimate cases, and disrupt key activities. Resistance to EDS reported in the health zones of Mandima, Nyakunde and Mambasa, and at AS Soliniama (ZS Bunia). - Response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, and increase the number of EDS teams.

Nord-Kivu capacity was not reported on 15/07 (129.6% at 14/07), raising admission delay and nosocomial-transmission risk. - Response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion and deploy temporary structures.
